Let's move down a bit, Mr. Poparic, and 3b says: "As a result of coming under fire" -- Effectively it says as a result of coming under fire while assisting small arms casualties, the UNPROFOR EgyBat anti-sniping team returned fire on Bosnian Serb army positions at Sharpstone. And then following this, it's about a third of the way through the paragraph, the UNMO Vogosca team received a telephone call from the commander of the Radava Battalion, Vogosca Brigade, Bosnian Serb army, saying that if the EgyBat APC in his target practice area wasn't moved within half an hour it would be fired on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, your quote from 3b is not very exact. You started saying: "As a result of coming under while assisting small arms ..." Whereas the original reads: "During the activity in the area of Sharpstone and the resulting casualties reported," there and there and there --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "... and the incident reported there." That's not exactly the same. Would you please keep that in mind. It may even have relevant difference of meaning here, I do not know. But what results from what is changed in your quote compared to the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm happy to repeat myself, Your Honour, if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you repeat what is written here rather than to repeat yourself, that would be appreciated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: "During the activity in the area of Sharpstone," giving some co-ordinates, "and the resulting casualties reported at paragraphs 8.a.ii and 8.a.iii and the incident reported at paragraph 3a," which is the one I previously read, "the EgyBat anti-sniping APC at that location returned fire onto BSA positions on Sharpstone. Following this retaliation, UNMO Vogosca team received a telephone call from the Commander Radava Battalion, Vogosca Brigade BSA at 061530 March 1995, stating that if the 'EgyBat APC in his target practice area (Sedrenik) is not removed within 30 minutes, it will be fired upon.' Shortly after this call the sector commander arrived at the APC location and the UNMO Vogosca team received another telephone call at 061550A March 95 from the Radava Battalion commander, stating that he would also fire upon the 'UNPROFOR reinforcements with the APC.' And the APC has subsequently been moved to a position where it can continue to monitor the Sharpstone feature." When you talk about exchange of fire, are you talking about exchange of fire between the warring factions?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see here that there was an exchange of gun-fire between members of UNPROFOR and the Army of Republika Srpska. I believe that there was an exchange between the warring parties, too. Because this kind of tense situation -- I mean, I don't see what was the reason for this kind of tense situation unless there had been some combat before that. So obviously this commander believed the observers from the Egyptian Battalion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, whatever you may believe that must have proceeded for reasons, is there any document which supports what you consider to be logic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this document supports that because I find it illogical that the commander of this battalion would be threatening the members of the Egyptian Battalion unless something had happened that he believed was irregular. Probably there was some kind of an exchange there. I mean, that's my assumption. I don't have any -- we see here, subparagraph a, even UNMO is not certain where the fire had come from. Their assumption is that it came from Spicasta Stijena. So in my view this was a complex situation and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you've answered my question. Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put then a follow-up question. I take you back to pages 51 and 52. Ms. Edgerton put to you what you said in the Karadzic trial, and I quote that part: "... in the Karadzic trial," according to Ms. Edgerton, you said "all the facts point to the conclusion that the victim was walking home from school through a substantial exchange of fire and shot as a result." In your following answer today, you said: "A major exchange," meaning of gun-fire. And then you say: "I don't know whether it happened at that particular moment, though." There is a major difference between the two, that this young man was shot as a result of exchange of fires. That suggests that you were sure that there was an exchange of gun-fire. Now you say: I don't know whether it happened at that particular moment. Which of the two is true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, according to the description of these things that happened, and we can see that from UNMO reports, et cetera, there was a very complex situation there and there was an exchange of gun-fire. Now, what happened at the moment when Tarik Zunic came up, that I don't have any information about. He just says that he heard firing from M74. There is no denying that. Now, what happened before that and how everything happened, I have no information about that. I mean, at least I don't have any information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why did you say in the Karadzic trial that there was a substantial exchange of fire and that the man was shot as a result when he was walking through this substantial exchange of fire? I take it from your answer -- the last answer that you don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, according to the reports a lot of ammunition had been used in that period. I mean -- when we say exchange of gun-fire, if one side opened fire, the other side does not have to respond immediately. I mean, they can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, Mr. Poparic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- now you are changing your evidence from the Karadzic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. I still think that there was an exchange of gun-fire. I mean, what preceded --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, it's a serious matter we are talking about. It was put to you that you said in the Karadzic trial: "The victim was walking home from school through a substantial exchange of fire and shot as a result." Do you stand by that or do you change it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stand by that because it is possible that before the boy reached that place, one side opened fire, then there was a brief lull before the other side responded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I stop you. No, I stop you. You say "it is possible." In the Karadzic case you didn't say that it is possible. You say he was walking through a substantial exchange of fire and shot as a result, without any reservation. That was a clear statement. If you say you stand by that, then it is not true what you said today, or the other way around. But I'm not insisting on that. I just put it on the record. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have a look at 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- 10408, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, this is the document that you cite at paragraph 237, footnote 468, in support of the following proposition: Due to combat operations, no onsite investigation was conducted. Only an Official Note was drawn up stating that at the Kosevo hospital they received information that this was a case of slight bodily injury, i.e., an entry-exit wound through the hand. Now, my question for you is: This document says nothing about combat operations, does it? It only refers to firing from the aggressor's positions at the place where Tarik Zunic was wounded. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a report of the police of Bosnia-Herzegovina. There is a reference here to the firing and the situation was such that they could not go to the site itself, which is not to say that the other side did not respond. That is their report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But do you have any information that the other side responded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably. If the gun-fire went on for so long that the -- they could not go out to the site, that means that something was going on all day. I don't think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- somebody would just be shooting randomly all day just like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am not asking you for probabilities. I have asked you if you have any information that the other side responded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't but there are probably some witnesses that spoke about this event and certainly know better about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, I'm not asking for probabilities. You don't have any information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I in more general terms invite you not -- always to make very clear where in your report you rely on what you considered a probability, and also in your answers to questions always be clear when you are talking about probabilities and when you are talking, which we expect you to do, about firm conclusions drawn on the basis of facts - not probabilities, facts - which are within the realm of your expertise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this document as a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 10408 receives Exhibit Number P7597.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just staying with Sedrenik for a little while, I'd like to talk for a second about Scheduled Incident F-2 which we've already had a little conversation about, Mr. Poparic. It's -- now, you've already explained in your cross-examination that you weren't at the actual incident location in this case because it was changed. But it's correct, isn't it, that despite the incident location being changed, you knew that the crime scene was still preserved? You knew that, right? You knew that the gouge mark where the victim -- the gouge mark that the bullet that hit the victim made on the house was still preserved; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when I was visiting, I didn't know that. What you are talking about is visible in the film made by Mr. Hogan. But at the time of my tour, I did not have that movie. That place that you are referring to is inside a room, inside a place with a fence around it, and I'm not quite sure that's the place where the bullet hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, in fact you had read the victim's witness statement, her statement of 25 July 2001, because you footnote it at footnotes 92 to 98 in your report and you would have seen that evidence in her statement that the gouge mark was still visible. So putting aside whenever you may have had Mr. Hogan's videos, you read the victim's statement and you knew from that the gouge mark was still visible; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read that but at the time -- the time when Mr. Hogan filmed and this other time don't coincide. There was a lot of construction material and debris in that place. I'm not quite sure, but I accept that what was filmed was the reality of the event. I have no reason to doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And I'd like to put to you that you also know, because you referred to the testimony of this witness on this point, you also know that in the Galic case she marked a photo showing a clear line of sight from the incident location to Spicasta Stijena. You know that.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the witness marked the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last sentence. The witness said something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can you repeat your last sentence?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept she marked the photograph. But this visibility that you are mentioning, we can talk about that. I'm not sure what's seen on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, have you seen -- you've seen the photograph, though, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is very far away from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you come a bit closer to the microphone, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So let's have a look at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, no speaking aloud. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So let's have a look at the photograph. It's 65 ter number 10476. If we can go to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, that's the photograph that we're talking about, isn't it, and that's the photograph referred to in the testimony you footnote to in paragraph 41 of your report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And it's your position, having read the evidence of the witness in the Galic case and not having been to the incident location -- no, let me ask this a different way. So this photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would object at this point. We discussed this whether this witness was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- at the scene or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you can object to a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But this is repetitious all the time. He did not go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think this was an introduction to a question, and if the question is objectionable, you may object and giving the reasons for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We object to this kind of introduction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That he did not visit the site, scene. He did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Ms. Edgerton may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So this photograph marked by the victim shows a clear and unobstructed line of sight from Spicasta Stijena to the incident location; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. First of all this photograph --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Stop --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was not taken --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, you answered my question. Now, when we talked about the line of sight in the Karadzic case, we -- I also showed you a photograph that was taken on 18 August 1996 of the area of Sedrenik from Spicasta Stijena on which you could clearly see victim's house. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let's have a look please at 65 ter number 33366. And may we go into private session and have this picture not broadcast, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to go on to another area for the rest of this session, and it's Nedzarici and the School for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the School for the Blind, if I have everything correct, is, Mr. Poparic, the alleged origin of fire for F-9, the shooting of Sanela Muratovic, the Unscheduled Incident of 24 October 1994 involving the shooting death of Adnan Kasapovic, which is an Unscheduled Incident you mention at paragraphs 247 to 252 and in your language 245 to 248. It's the location you allege as the origin of fire for an incident that appears in your Annex 6 on 15 May 1995 at paragraphs -- I'll check the page reference, but -- for B/C/S, but in English I have paragraphs 18 to 22. And it's also the alleged origin of fire for your Unscheduled Incident 9, which is also from Annex 6 of your report. So first of all, I just want to deal briefly with the sniping of Stefan Bijelac, which is your Unscheduled Incident 3 from Annex 6, English pages 333 to 336. Take your time. I apologise, I don't have the page references in your language here for you -- oh, maybe I do. 316 to 318, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incident number 3, right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Okay. In this incident, your only source of information is the investigative file; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let's have a look at it. It's our 65 ter number 33149. Here we've got it on the screen in front of us. Now, you've looked at this file, as you said, and so you can confirm, I think, that the investigative report for this incident says absolutely nothing about the origin of fire as being the School for the Blind; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it says from the aggressor's position in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't see the words "School for the Blind" anywhere in this document; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be marked as a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 33149 receives Exhibit Number P7600.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, as I read through your report and I heard your evidence in this case, you make an assertion that seems to me kind of fundamental to all the remaining incidents apart from this 15 May one, and that is that no one ever presented evidence to you that there was a firing position at the School for the Blind although the place was inspected after the Dayton Accords. And you said that at T 40494 in this case. You said: "I never received anything that would indicate to me that this was an arranged firing position." So you stand by that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I never received such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let's have a look, please, at 65 ter number 32782.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So this is a photo from a video still of the School for the Blind, and I showed it to you in the Karadzic case. And it's taken, by the way, from 65 ter number 33269, which is a film made in 1996 after the reintegration. Now, we talked about this photo in the Karadzic case, and you've adopted this photo and incorporated it into your report; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, when we talked about this photo in the Karadzic case, I showed you a document about sniping from the School for the Blind, and it's P1065.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we look at that, please. We can go over to page 5 in English and page 6 in the B/C/S, paragraph number 2b. Actually, I've got my letters wrong, it's 2d .

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Where it says: "UNMOs confirm from the spot as well as hospital visit 1 times Bosnian civ," I presume you mean a civilian, "male, age 17, injured by sniping at co-ordinates BP 863578 near the house for the blind people at Alipasino Polje area," giving the date, 111530 B July 1994. "It is suspected in the sniping came from and co-ordinates BP 859578 BSA side. It may be highlighted that this is the third casualty, all civilians, in the same spot in the last few days." So this document reports sniping near the house for the blind people. It's three weeks after incident F-9 and it reports at least one sniping being the third casualty in the same spot in the last few days. This doesn't indicate to you that there was a firing position of the Army of Republika Srpska in the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report coincides with my assertion that it was not a firing position at the School for the Blind. It wasn't there but it was in the vicinity. The report also says near the School for the Blind --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I see, nobody is claiming --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just seek to clarify this, Witness. The report, as far as I can read it, says that the person was injured near to the School of the Blind. I think it doesn't say that much about a sniping position because usually the victims are not exactly where the shooters are, isn't it. If they are shot nearby, it could be any place which is nearby including the School of the Blind. Is that -- is that a interpretation you would follow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was near the School for the Blind. You're right. When we look at it more carefully, you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you also said that this supports that it was not a sniping position. Could you explain how someone being injured in the vicinity of a certain building, that that would support your assumption that it would not have come from that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not my assumption. It just says here that it's not from the building. It's certain that it was near it. In my report, I maintain that the firing position was somewhere near that building. It was close and it's visible from the trace and the surrounding buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would accept that to be a firing place only if the person was shot at that building itself. Is that how I have to understand your logic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, certainly not. The discussion here is whether there was a firing position on that building. I did not see any document that would persuade me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But there was a firing position near that building. It's visible from the traces of the exchange of fire on both sides, and I put that in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you've still not explained to me why -- if a person is shot nearby a building, why that supports your position that that person was not shot at from that building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, then you misunderstood me. I base that assertion on all the knowledge that I had which indicates that a firing position of the VRS was somewhere close to that building. We showed that in the examination-in-chief where it could be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you're telling me now is that you had other information which would support your position, which I understand. But I leave it to that. Please proceed. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a translation issue in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that I shouldn't raise it in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have -- we take a break in eight minutes from now. Could you raise it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When he leaves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- when he leaves the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When he leaves --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, we leave it to that and that perhaps put this document for a second aside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I have a clarification question to ask here. It looks like -- and I don't know whether it will resolve the translation issue. Sir, in your discussion with Judge Orie, Judge Orie tells you and reads from this document that the person injured was near -- was injured near the house for the blind. You keep saying the firing came from near the house. Therefore, it couldn't come from the house. Just look at the document and see that it is -- it doesn't talk about the firing being near the house but it talks about --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- the injured person being injured near the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is -- from Mr. Lukic, I understand this is the translation issue which should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But if he clarifies my question, then there is no need for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll first later hear about the translation issue, where after Judge Moloto may still have further questions on the matter. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You're not disputing, though, are you, that there were VRS positions in the School for the Blind? You accept that, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Asked and answered several times. He does dispute that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you're supposed not to -- to repeat the answer. Do you dispute that there were positions?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I may. And I distinguish "military positions" from "firing positions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were there any Bosnian Serb soldiers in the -- I take it that you're -- Ms. Edgerton, that you are talking about Bosnian Serb soldiers. Was there any military presence in the School of the Blind from the Bosnian Serb side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that in the direct examination. Yes. On the ground floor there were troops who were deployed there, but the firing position itself was not inside the building. It was further away, which I established from the traces of an exchange of fire. In fact, traces on both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it may be clear that you were a bit early with your intervention. I see that you're accepting that. Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So let's have a look at another document, P1079. And I think we should go to page 4, if I'm not mistaken, in both languages. Paragraph 24b.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So here, on 13 July 1994, is UNPROFOR reporting that the commander of the 1st Battalion of the Bosnian Serb Army Ilidza Brigade "admitted the sniping by BSA from BP 859578 (house for blind people). He promised that there would be no more sniping from that place." So here's a specific admission from an SRK military commander that there was sniping from the School for the Blind. Now, does that indicate to you that there was a firing position of the VRS in that building sniping civilians?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that this commander admitted that somebody opened fire from the Institute for the Blind, but that still doesn't prove that this was a proper firing position that was operating all the time. Perhaps this was sporadic gun-fire that somebody opened from this building.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So on the basis of this document, you're now prepared to accept that there was firing from the School for the Blind; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One case was registered here.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: How much more is it going to take, Mr. Poparic? Let me show you 65 ter number 33205.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the document we just looked at, Mr. Poparic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let's go over to page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, this is a record of the testimony of the victim in this case, Sanela Muratovic, given to the Cantonal Court in Sarajevo in the trial of Goran Vasic in April of 1998. And she says at the bottom of the largest paragraph: "... I know snipers fired very frequently from that place. On that spot, I could show you the place where I was hit. I can also indicate the position and the direction I was facing when I was injured." Here's some evidence from the victim of repeated, frequent sniper fire from the School for the Blind. Are you prepared to accept it now?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just take a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's just part of the sentence. The whole sentence should be read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to read the whole sentence. If you follow the suggestion, Ms. Edgerton, we'll hear from you. Otherwise, Mr. Lukic will deal with it in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The sentence, if I understand correctly -- I apologise for the delay.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: "I have the medical documentation and enclose it herewith. In that section, the sniper fired very often from the direction of Nedzarici and this bullet also came from the direction of Nedzarici - I would say from the Institute for the Blind - and I know snipers fired very frequently from that place." And I don't think I need to bother repeating the last line. So maybe I should repeat my question: What's it going to take, Mr. Poparic? Are you now prepared to accept evidence that there was an SRK sniping position in the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please speak into the microphone and could you repeat your answer, Witness. Witness, could you -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of this document, I am not prepared to accept that. Because the way she described this incident, that is roughly the way Medina Omerovic, her friend, described it. They were walking from Djure Jaksica Street and she was hit. I analysed that incident and she certainly could not have been hit from the Institute of the Blind. She was hit by a ricochetted bullet, a bullet that ricochetted off Djure Jaksica number 17, that building. What she is stating here, I mean, I don't know how she came to this information, where this fire was opened from. But she was not wounded by fire that came from the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this as a Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours, just before we break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 33205 receives Exhibit Number P7601, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. We'll take a break. I take it that this is a suitable moment. You may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, can we -- if we have P01065 on our screens again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's about the translation issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. And we need page 5 in English and page 6 in B/C/S version, please. If we see under d. in B/C/S, my understanding that here this BP is for sniper. And I will read in B/C/S so you get the translation. After brackets, and I quote in B/C/S: [Interpretation] "... wounded when fire was opened from a sniper at BP 863578 near the Institute for the Blind at Alipasino Polje." [In English] So in B/C/S it looks like it was described as sniper was on this BP, Your Honour. That's why that this maybe created confusion, since the English the authoritative for you but witness was probably reading in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. And you could have explained that to me when I asked the question and that would have cleared -- avoided the need to you to explain. That's all I was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And if we go to the next sentence, it is clear what the document says in English: "It is suspected that the sniping came from," and then there is a specific position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The same number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the same number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 578 -- no, this is 8595. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the number --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The three last numbers are the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number is not the same. You know that part of the number always goes for the horizontal and the other for the vertical. So apparently these are different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Still in B/C/S it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In B/C/S are the numbers the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- it looks like both are for sniper somehow. I don't know. That's how I understand. Maybe somebody could understand it to mean differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We may address that matter after the break. We'll take a break and we'll resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Yes, Mr. Tieger, you wanted to raise a matter in the absence of the witness or?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Either way, Mr. President, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. This is in connection with the upcoming cross-examination of expert Kovac whose report spans all three of the components in this case. The Prosecution recently spoke with the Defence about its proposal -- or our proposal that for efficiency of both preparation and presentation, that two Prosecution counsel with expertise in different areas of the case participate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The Defence has no objection to this proposal. And while we anticipate that the Trial Chamber would not either, we wanted of course to alert you to that and confirm that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although not very common, it's no problem for the Chamber, especially since it's not a problem to the Defence, that -- that the evidence will be elicited by two counsel. Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Have you ever seen, Mr. Poparic, any military documents from either of the warring factions that would -- that show -- that would show -- or with evidence of a firing position in the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any such evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the document we saw last before the break has disappeared from the screen. Can we get that back. I would like to raise one matter with respect to that document. It may have been P7601. No, it's not that one. No, it must be P1065, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The suggestion is that it would be P1065. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And can we go back to the page we had on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was page 5 in both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And now we need the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 6 in B/C/S, 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 6 in B/C/S, 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, I take you back to the sentence under 2d which was read out to you by Ms. Edgerton, but there is one sentence: "It is suspected that the sniping came from BP 859578 BSA side." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Try to remember this number and -- when we go back to P1079, page 4, paragraph 24b. So in this UNPROFOR report, we see under 24b -- perhaps this is going to the next page in B/C/S, that: "It was admitted that the sniping by BSA came from BP 859578," then in brackets, "(house for blind people)." I take it that this is the same number now with an addition that it should be the house for blind people? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I have to explain. These co-ordinates show a broader area; that is to say, that house or, rather, this Institute for the Blind is in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would need one more decimal digit in order to have the exact location of the building. This is a broader area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How large is it, could you tell us? How large is that area which is covered by these six digits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these co-ordinates -- I mean, well, this co-ordinate is a square, if I can call it that, of a thousand metres. So then there is 85, between 85 and 86. I mean, 900 metres and then 800 metres, and then this other one between 57 and 58, that's roughly around the eighth part. I can check. I can check on that map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- just explain this six-digit number, does it cover what kind of -- how large is the area which is covered by this number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, this area is the ninth point of 85, 86, so then this co-ordinate is divided into 10. And then the one that divides it into the ninth part is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm asking you as an expert irrespective of which number we are talking about. A six-digit number, how large is the area which is covered by six-digit number, whatever number it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this number, this six-digit number does give an intersection. Now, whether it is exactly at the building of the Institute of the Blind, I cannot confirm that. I would have to check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said it is a broader area. How big is the area covered by a six-digit number? I'm asking you as an expert. If you don't know, then tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I rushed a bit with my answer. There are six digits here and there is an intersection of two lines, so there is one point that is denoted by this co-ordinate. So I would have to check whether it is actually the Institute of the Blind. If it were four, then it would to be a broader area than 1.000 metres by 1.000 metres, so I would have to check whether it corresponds to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, there is nothing to check. It is an intersection of two lines and this is a specific spot. According to the UNPROFOR report, it is the house for the blind people; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to their report, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, still I do not have an answer to the question. With six digits, is that -- does that describe an area by 10 by 10 metres, 100 by 100 metres, 1 kilometre by 1 kilometre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When we have this with six digits, then it's one point. It is an intersection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if you were to see military documents from either of the warring factions, what kind of weight would you give to military documents?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to answer now what kind of weight I'd give. It depends on what was written in them, what they say. I'd need to see these documents. I cannot say anything in advance.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does it depend on which one of the warring factions generated the document?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It depends on the basis on which something is claimed in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a military document, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: 65 ter number 33221. So this is a Main Staff report for the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina dated 25 August 1992 on the security situation in the republic. And I'd like us to go over to English page 4 and B/C/S page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So in your language, I'd like you to have a look at the -- pretty much the eleventh line down in the first paragraph. And in the English, it's the top of the first paragraph. And it says, as of the date of the report: "As of 5:15, the enemy carried the fire over to the settlement itself," referring to Vojnicko Polje, in the sentence immediately preceding, "shelling it for two hours. Activities were also manifested in the sector of the Aleksa Santic School. A PAM was concurrently firing from the sector of the school, Dom Slijepih, centre for the blind, towards Dzemela Bijedica Street and the student dormitories." What's a PAM?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft gun, 12.7 calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So here is a military document, a security report from the ABiH Main Staff that says VRS forces are firing an anti-aircraft gun from the sector of the School for the Blind. Do you accept that VRS force -- based on this document, are you now prepared to accept that VRS forces were firing from positions in the area of the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says from the region of school, from the area of school, not from the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's comment rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what -- yes, but in the question the word "area" is not repeated, but it's comment rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document, it says that fire was opened from the area of the Institute for the Blind towards Dzemela Bijedica Street and the student dormitories. That's correct. I claimed that in the area of that school there were certainly certain positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this as a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Lukic, Ms. Edgerton -- I didn't have my transcript opened at that moment but she said exactly what the document says. She was talking about the area. Not positions in the School of the Blind but positions at the area of the School of the Blind. Therefore, I think that should have led me to say that, first of all, it's a comment; and second, that it was an inaccurate comment. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 33221 receives Exhibit Number P7602.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to go to 65 ter number 33220, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, this is dated 27 January 1993 and it's a report from the 1st Corps -- or to the 1st Corps command on the situation in their area of responsibility. Now, in both languages if you can just stay on the first page, go all the way down to the entry on the bottom in English and the entry on the bottom of -- the entry fifth from the bottom in B/C/S. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Edgerton, do we know corps command of which army?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That would be the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, it says at 11 -- it reports on enemy activities at 11.00 and it says: "Sniper activity from the centre for the blind targeting Aleja B. Bujica Street." So here a contemporaneous military document reporting sniper activity from the School for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And actually if we go over to the next page in English I just want to see if there is a sentence that's been cut off -- no. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So to go back to my question. Here is a contemporaneous military document reporting sniper activity by VRS forces for the School for the Blind. Are you now, based on this document, prepared to accept that VRS snipers operated from the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no information here that would convince me that it was exactly from the School for the Blind. It could be near the School for the Blind and then the person who is observing would think it was from the school, but it's a fact that this is written.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So your answer is no. Despite what's written in this document, you're still not prepared --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can you not interrupt me, please. You're still not prepared to accept that VRS snipers operated from the School for the Blind; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept that it is written here, but I don't have the elements to conclude that it was exactly from the School for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this as a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 33220 receives Exhibit Number P7603.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, do you accept that there is a clear and obstructed -- unobstructed, pardon me, a clear and unobstructed line of sight from the School for the Blind to the incident location for F-9?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from one part of the School for the Blind there is such a view. One small part of the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that's on the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the fact that I was there, it was recorded, and it is shown. You can see one part, the top ten windows. It's here on the picture 124 in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, can I just clarify something. You said just now that you were there, but at the beginning of your cross-examination you said you've never been inside the School for the Blind; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So you're prepared to accept that there is a small line of sight on the basis of this picture from the video still? Am I correct in understanding that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought -- I'm not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it a small line of sight or is it a line of sight from a small area of the school?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Ah-ha. A line of sight from one small part of the school. I stand corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like you to have a look at a picture that was taken from inside the School for the Blind in 1996, and it's taken from the same video that you've pulled the picture that appears as image 123 of -- in your report. It's 65 ter number 33333. So, Mr. Poparic, however big the part of the school might be that has a line of sight, you're prepared to accept it's not obstructed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just take a look. Yes, there are obstacles. I think this is a garage here in front and it obstructs part of the area in front of the building, if I'm not mistaken. I don't find the picture very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Fine. I have more to show you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the witness please indicate where is a garage? I don't see it. Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I put a letter to mark it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There is only one marking and you indicate here that in your view this is a garage; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question would be from which point does this garage obstruct the view? Where is the person looking supposed to be positioned?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I take it that's a question for Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just draw. As far as I can see, the angle is not very convenient. It should be between these two buildings. Down here, in that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You pointed to that by an arrow from up to down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the road, which is not visible from here, that's where it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And where is the observer supposed to be having a line of sight to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This building on the left, if I'm not mistaken, is in the Djure Jaksica Street. Behind it should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I stop you there. Listen to my question. Where is the observer supposed to be looking at to get the garage to be an obstruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person who's looking from this window sees this building in Djure Jaksica Street with a red facade, if I'm right. And the next building is number 17. Those two girls stood behind the trench between these two buildings. The angle is shifted a bit, so it's not quite clear. Between this white building and the red wall, that's where the girls were standing at the trench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But the garage is not between the white building and the red building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's close to the School for the Blind. It's a two-storey building with a garage below.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just listen to my question. The garage is not between the white building and the red building. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So if the girls were standing in front of the red building, the garage is not obstructing the person who is observes from where the arrow is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's an obstacle because the garage is taller. We don't see the road in that street, so these two girls could not be visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you tendering this marked document, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm going to come back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to do it right now --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- otherwise if it disappears from the screen ...

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Oh, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a photograph marked by the witness is admitted into evidence. Ms. Edgerton, could you assist me from where, in what direction is this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I -- to speak perfectly accurately, Your Honour, I can't do it from memory. I would prefer to check exactly and revert to you with that information first thing tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. And if you can link it in one way or another to image 123 in the witness's report, then that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honours, in the few moments we have left, I'd like to go to some of the images in the witness's report. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there is one minute left. I can't imagine that you would be able to do that within that one minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, it would take me about five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we would adjourn for the day. Mr. Poparic, we would like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.30 in the morning. And I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether given last week or today or still to be given tomorrow or the days to come. If that's clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 3rd of November, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of November, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
